family_notes.translation: Younger bilingual family members (Justin and Dad) translate for grandparents on-site. Tour/destination language availability is a soft comfort factor, not a blocking factor — do not exclude a destination on language grounds alone.

mobility_rules.description: Strong preferences to weigh heavily when ranking itinerary candidates — not absolute blocking rules. A destination that stretches one of these can still be worth surfacing if it's otherwise an excellent fit; flag the tradeoff instead of silently excluding it.

budget_rules.roi_logic: Favor options where per-person cost-per-day is reasonable relative to trip uniqueness/duration AND mobility_rules are largely satisfiable at the destination. A cruise bundles lodging+food+transport into one fixed cost with near-zero daily walking, which is why it clears the bar at a higher price. A beach destination at the same price with high heat/humidity and long transit is a weaker fit even under budget — but note it as an option with caveats rather than refusing to mention it.
roi_reflections: Fixed-cost trips (cruises, all-inclusive) tolerate a higher price ceiling because they remove daily walking/transit variability.
A la carte city-hopping itineraries should stay closer to the soft cap since walking and layover risk compound across stops.

precedent_examples.reason: Fixed-cost cruise, minimal daily walking, bilingual shore excursions available, temperate climate in shoulder season.
High summer humidity and limited bilingual tour operators made this a weaker fit — not a hard rule violation, just lower ROI at that price.

regional_travel_history.usage_note: Reference context only — never use this to hard-exclude a destination. De-prioritize visited/repetitive and low-interest/unsafe regions relative to new, unique high-priority regions, but still mention them if the user asks directly.
